newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ex-official denies guilt in HIV blood deaths.
newsitem.headline: Japan ex-official denies guilt in HIV blood deaths.

text.p: A former Japanese Health Ministry bureaucrat pleaded not guilty on Wednesday to professional negligence charges in his trial for the death of two patients who were given HIV-tainted blood products.

Akihito Matsumura, former head of the ministry's Health and Service Bureau, told the Tokyo District Court he was not responsible for the AIDS deaths of a haemophiliac and a liver ailment patient, who were treated with tainted blood products in the mid-1980s.
"I did not idly neglect the situation. I believe I committed no negligence," Matsumura, 55, told the opening session.
He is the second major figure to go on trial for a scandal involving allegations of a government cover-up and unethical links between bureaucrats and drug firms in the 1980s.

On Monday, Takeshi Abe, who was Japan's leading authority on haemophilia and AIDS, pleaded not guilty to charges of professional negligence in the death of a young haemophiliac who had contracted AIDS through unheated blood products.
The professional negligence charge carries a maximum five-year prison sentence.

Matsumura, as head of the ministry's Biologics and Antibiotics Division, failed to stop the sale of blood products that had not been heat-treated, knowing they could carry HIV, the virus that causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), the prosecution said.
Matsumura was in charge of blood products between July 1984 and June 1986.

Prosecutors said he knew the risk of imported unheated blood products by November 1984 after Japanese researchers submitted reports that showed six of 27 haemophiliacs surveyed had tested positive for HIV.

They alleged that even after heated blood products were put on sale in December 1985 following the ministry's approval six months earlier, Matsumura failed to halt sales of unheated blood products or recall them.
About 1,800 of Japan's estimated 5,000 haemophiliacs contracted the AIDS-causing virus in the 1980s through unheated blood-clotting agents imported from the United States.
Four hundred of the HIV-infected hemophiliacs have since died.
On March 24, three former presidents of Green Cross Corp., an Osaka-based main supplier of blood products, will also enter pleas at their first court hearings for the scandal.

Green Cross, which this month said it would be merged in October into drug maker Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries, supplied the blood products used to treat the liver disease patient whose death Matsumura is being held accountable for, prosecutors said.
